assumptions: large-scale studies primarily report significance rather than estimation
conclusion: The method seeks to connect effect estimation and testing through sign-error probabilities because large-scale studies commonly emphasize testing alone.
scope: Motivation for posterior effect summaries and lfsr.
span: However, despite ongoing interest in this area from both frequentist (Benjamini and Yekutieli, 2005) and Bayesian (Zhao and Gene Hwang, 2012; Gelman and others, 2012) perspectives, in practice large-scale studies that assess many effects almost invariably focus on testing significance and controlling the FDR, and not on estimation. To help provide a bridge between FDR and estimation we introduce the term “local false sign rate” (lfsr), which is analogous to the “local false discovery rate” (lfdr) (Efron, 2008), but which measures confidence in the sign of each effect rather than confidence in each effect being non-zero.
